svg.data-vd-play-label: Play: meet the white blood cells
svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "A stained blood smear: red cells, platelets and five kinds of white blood cell."], [1, "Neutrophils: lobed nucleus; phagocytes."], [4, "Lymphocytes: large round nucleus; B cells release antibodies."], [7, "Monocytes become macrophages."], [9.5, "Eosinophils and basophils are rare; they act in parasite infections, allergy and inflammation."], [12.5, "Typical proportions of white blood cells."]]
svg.title: White blood cells
svg.desc: A blood smear showing neutrophils, lymphocytes, a monocyte, an eosinophil and a basophil among red cells and platelets, with their roles and typical percentages.
svg.text: As seen in a stained blood smear (Wright/Giemsa stain colours). Not to scale with each other.

g.data-info: Red cells (no nucleus) carry oxygen; platelets are cell fragments that help blood clot. About 700 red cells for every white cell.
Multi-lobed nucleus, granular cytoplasm. The most common white blood cell: a phagocyte that engulfs bacteria.
Large round nucleus with a thin rim of cytoplasm. B lymphocytes make antibodies; T lymphocytes help them and kill infected cells.
The largest white cell, with a kidney-shaped nucleus. Leaves the blood and becomes a macrophage (phagocyte); presents antigens.
Two-lobed nucleus and red-orange granules. Attacks parasites and is involved in allergies.
Dark blue-purple granules hide the nucleus. Releases histamine in inflammation and allergy.
